analysis.evidence: Pharaoh gives orders to אֲנָשִׁים, “men,” concerning Abram (עָלָיו). The next verb, וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ, tells what the men did in response: they sent Abram away with his wife and all he had.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ־ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Pharaoh as its subject.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְצַו עָלָיו פַּרְעֹה אֲנָשִׁים, Pharaoh gives orders to the men concerning Abram. The next clause describes the men carrying out those orders by sending him away.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with a third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix referring to Abram.

evidence.note: שָׂרֵי פַרְעֹה identifies the men who see Sarai as Pharaoh’s officials.
מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם identifies Pharaoh as king of Egypt.

article.name: פַּרְעֹה
article.summary: Pharaoh is the royal title by which the text names the king of Egypt. In Abram’s time, Pharaoh’s officials see Sarai and praise her to him.

draft.change: Add a name entry for the royal title פַּרְעֹה and correct the supplied gloss “lye; potash” for this occurrence.
draft.definition: Pharaoh, the title used to designate the king of Egypt.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:15 identifies Pharaoh through his officials and his household. Exodus 6:11 explicitly calls him פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם, “Pharaoh king of Egypt.”

analysis.evidence: Pharaoh gives the order expressed by the singular verb וַיְצַו. The men he commands, אֲנָשִׁים, then send Abram away with his wife and possessions, as the plural verb וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ indicates.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun, a royal title used as a name. It has no prefix or suffix and is the subject of וַיְצַו.
analysis.sense: The king of Egypt, designated by his royal title.

analysis.evidence: Pharaoh gives the men orders concerning Abram. The following plural verb וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ, ‘and they sent away’, identifies those men as the ones who sent Abram, his wife, and his possessions on their way.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute. אֲנָשִׁים is the irregular plural of אִישׁ.

analysis.evidence: Pharaoh gives orders to אֲנָשִׁים, the men who then carry them out. The direct objects name whom and what they send on their way together: Abram (אֹתוֹ), his wife, and all that belongs to him.
analysis.gloss: and they sent him on his way
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol. The יְ־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural.
